focus: Data visualization, statistics, statistical analysis, and reproducible scientific computing
title: Reading Networks Without Losing the Plot
utility_use_case: A research team has paired measurements of instrument temperature and signal intensity in a CSV file. Before fitting a richer model, a scientist runs `bash correlation-report.sh --file measurements.csv --x temperature --y intensity` to obtain a reproducible descriptive summary and fitted line. They then inspect a scatterplot, check for outliers and nonlinear patterns, and decide whether the association warrants further analysis. The report is not treated as a significance test or evidence that temperature causes changes in intensity.

editorial_review.summary: Corrected the directed-graph closeness convention and distinguished the articulation point D from a bridge edge. The worked numeric examples and utility documentation agree with the supplied data and executable source.

edits.old: A common form is the reciprocal of the mean distance from a node to all other nodes.
edits.new: In an undirected graph, a common form is the reciprocal of the mean distance to all other nodes. In a directed graph, definitions may use distances from or to the node.

edits.old: act as a bridge between parts of the network.
edits.new: serve as an articulation point between parts of the network.
